Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleMedia Corp Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your telephone keypad if you would like to join the queue. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleMedia Corp's Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q4 2023. We exceeded expectations in several key areas. First, our adjusted EBITDA margin expanded meaningfully to 38.5%, reflecting strong operational leverage. Second, free cash flow hit $3.6 billion in the quarter and $12.8 billion for the full year, providing substantial flexibility. Third, our enterprise and B2B initiatives delivered $1.2 billion in revenue, up 32% year-over-year with key contract wins. Fourth, blended churn improved to 1.12% monthly, driven by bundling and network enhancements. Finally, we are strategically positioning ourselves for cost of revenue efficiencies that supported margin gains while investing in growth.

We are seeing very positive results from our investments in 5G standalone architecture and our TeleStream Hub platform, and its impact on ARPU and retention is significant. Our focus on fiber expansion and media convergence continues to pay off, positioning us strongly for 2024.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $30.7 billion, up 4.1% year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $11.8 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.5%. We are maintaining strict cost discipline. Capital expenditures were $3.9 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion.

Good morning again, team. Let me dive deeper into our EBITDA margin performance, which stands as a key pillar of our financial strength in this capital-heavy telecom and media environment. For Q4, our adjusted EBITDA margin grew to 38.5%, an increase of 250 basis points from the prior year and 120 basis points from Q3. For the full year 2023, we achieved 37.2%, up 140 basis points from 35.8% in 2022. This represents our best annual expansion since we ramped up 5G commercialization in 2021, highlighting the benefits of our operational overhaul.

Breaking it down, revenue mix shifts provided about 180 basis points of uplift, led by wireless and broadband, which make up 65% of revenue. Postpaid ARPU rose 4.2% year-over-year to $58.30, powered by Unlimited Max 5G offerings and add-ons like TeleMedia+ streaming, now at 18 million subscribers with ad-tier reach comparable to leading services in major markets. Fixed wireless access reached 2.5 million homes, adding $15 in ARPU per user with 85% gross margins from minimal added capex. In media, direct-to-consumer platforms like TeleStream Hub improved content margins to 42% from 39%, aided by AI dynamic ad insertion that lifted CPMs 12% even in a weak linear TV ad environment.

Cost efficiencies contributed another 220 basis points. Network opex dropped to 18.2% of revenue from 20.1%, thanks to virtualizing 40% of our core from legacy EPC to cloud-native 5G SA, achieving cost savings similar to early Open RAN successes but through Nokia and Rakuten Symphony collaborations. We shut down 15% of 3G/4G sites, cutting $450 million yearly in power and upkeep, while AI traffic management trimmed energy expenses 22% against 15% global inflation. SG&A fell 300 basis points to 12.5% of revenue via zero-based budgeting and shifting 20% of customer care to Latin American nearshore sites, where monthly churn improved to 1.1% below the 1.6% industry average.

By region, North America, 55% of EBITDA, reached 41.2% margins, up 300 basis points, leveraging 75% C-band utilization from our $8 billion auction for 2 Gbps speeds and premium rates. Europe, 25% of EBITDA, was at 34.8% amid Gigabit Infrastructure Act wholesale rules, offset by MVNO partnerships adding $200 million in high-margin wholesale like Vodafone models. APAC and emerging markets, 20%, rose to 32.5% from 29%, boosted by 5G FWA in India and Indonesia akin to Jio strategies, gaining 10 million subs despite BSNL pricing.

These results affirm our Margin First strategy, mixing acquisitions like the $12 billion StreamNet content deal adding 400 basis points to media margins, with organic plays like edge computing for gaming and AR/VR, eyed for $1 billion high-margin revenue by 2025. Capex eased to 16.5% of revenue from 19%, with 5G ROIC at 14% above our 12% WACC, aiding deleveraging to 2.6x net debt/EBITDA.

For FY 2024, we expect 39-40.5% margins, or 180-280 basis points growth, assuming steady FX and no big auctions. Watch for OTT cord-cutting at 8%, countered by bundles, and U.S. rural subsidy shifts post-BEAD. With 85% 5G SA in top 100 MSAs and GenAI cutting faults 30%, we aim for 40%+ margins like diversified T-Mobile paths.

Now, shifting to free cash flow generation and how we're deploying it, a vital element of our balance sheet resilience. For FY 2023, we produced $12.8 billion in FCF, up 18% from $10.9 billion in 2022. Q4 alone delivered $3.6 billion, 22% above Q3's $2.95 billion and 25% year-over-year, as capex moderated after intense 5G builds and high-margin wireless/broadband cash flows accelerated.

FCF derives from operating cash flow minus capex. Adjusted OCF hit $28.4 billion yearly, 12% growth, with wireless at $16.2 billion up 15% from 4.2% postpaid ARPU to $58.50, 2.1 million net adds mostly 5G, and churn at 0.82%. FWA added 1.8 million subs and $1.2 billion OCF using C-band like Verizon's approach. Media & Entertainment gave $7.1 billion OCF, steady but margins to 42% with 45 million StreamHub paid users up 8%, AVOD up 35% via NFL rights and AI recommendations lifting engagement 22%. Enterprise added $5.1 billion, up 10%, from AWS edge deals and private 5G for industry.

Capex totaled $15.6 billion, down 14% from 2022's $18.1 billion, tapering 5G SA cores: 42% or $6.5 billion wireless for refarming/mmWave in top MSAs; 28% or $4.4 billion broadband for FTTH to 55% coverage at 10G PON vs. AT&T Fiber; 18% or $2.8 billion media for CDN/cloud to sub-5ms latency; rest maintenance/enterprise. U.S. 72% at $11.2 billion, Europe 18% via Vodafone JV for gigabit, APAC/LATAM 10% rural FWA.

Utilization-wise, $12.8 billion split balanced: 45% or $5.8 billion deleveraging to 2.3x EBITDA from 2.7x, including $4.2 billion debt paydowns at 4.1% average. Shareholder returns 35% or $4.5 billion: $2.8 billion dividends up 8% to $0.65/share yielding 3.2%, $1.7 billion buybacks retiring 2.1% shares at $42 average vs. 7.2x EV/FCF multiple below peers' 9x. Growth reinvestment 15% or $1.9 billion: $750 million Southeast fiber tuck-in for 20 million 10G homes, $450 million APAC Sub6 spectrum for Indonesia. Cash built to $8.2 billion for 5% buffer, eyeing content or Open RAN.

This FCF edge stems from 5G enterprise at 25%+ margins, media cash positive. Future capex targets ROI>15%: AI spectrum sharing saves 12% opex, LATAM FWA like Claro, FAST channels vs. 5% pay-TV drop. FY 2024 FCF guided $14.2-14.8 billion, 11-16% up, capex $14.5-15.0 billion mostly maintenance/growth, backing dividends, $5B+ buybacks, 2.2x debt, 6G/spectrum.

Next, on enterprise and B2B growth initiatives, a core driver as it hit 28% of Q4 revenue, up from 24% last year, shifting to high-margin recurring amid consumer softness. Revenues reached $1.2 billion, 32% year-over-year and 9% sequential growth, beating company 4.1% pace via Connect & Scale.

Key areas: 5G Enterprise Suite with private networks/slicing deployed 150+ sites YTD, up 75%, mid-band C-band ARPU $45,000/site from AR/VR manufacturing/logistics. Highlight: $250 million 5-year U.S. auto OEM deal like Ford/GM, $50 million ARR Q4 start, 55%+ EBITDA.

SD-WAN/SASE grew 42% to $450 million, SecureEdge at 4,200 customers, <1.2% churn vs. Cisco/VMware. Microsoft Azure hybrid edge cuts latency 40% for clouds. EMEA up 55% to $320 million GDPR-ready; €180 million (~$195 million) bank deal like Barclays/Deutsche for 50,000 seats UK/Germany/France, $40 million ARR.

Media & Content Delivery $350 million, +25%, edge CDN handles 15% U.S. primetime, 8K ABR cuts buffering 60%. APAC 38% growth $120 million; $120 million 3-year Asian OTT like Tencent for SEA sports, $40 million ARR, $50 billion market by 2027 per Omdia.

LATAM $150 million, 12.5%, up 45% fiber expansions Brazil/Mexico; $85 million telco dark fiber like Zayo.

B2B 65% ARR, 85% multi-year 4.2-year average, $18 billion pipeline up 40%, 35% near-term healthcare/retail. Our 20-30% TCO edge vs. Verizon/AT&T public RAN plus media fusion. Q4 tuck-ins eyed for SASE.

Q4 guide $1.3-1.4 billion, 28-35% growth, FY 30%+, EBITDA $5.8-6.0 billion, margins to 48% from 44%.

Turning to churn rate analysis, a vital metric for lifetime value in telecom and media. Blended monthly churn was 1.12% in Q4, down 10 bps QoQ from 1.22%, 18 bps YoY from 1.30%, annualizing to 13.2% below 15-18% peer benchmarks like Verizon/Comcast amid cord-cutting.

By segment: postpaid wireless 0.85%, -8 bps QoQ/-15 bps YoY, sticky 5G bundles with Paramount+/Peacock perks; fixed broadband 1.45%, -12 bps QoQ flat YoY post-fiber; StreamHub 4.2% quarterly (~1.4% monthly), better than Netflix via telco content.

Trend: down from Q4'22 1.28%, Q1'23 1.25%, Q2 1.22%, Q3 1.12%—16 bps best-in-class vs. AT&T 1.4%, T-Mobile. Q4 seasonal hold <1.20%. Curve flattened post-2022 1.45% inflation peak via retention.

Drivers: headwinds 40%—T-Mobile Go5G price wars 5-7 bps prepaid; 3.2% unemployment/2.5% inflation 15% broadband; legacy congestion 20 bps <100Mbps peaks OTT; media fatigue 10 bps strikes.

Tailwinds 60%—Total Connect bundle 25% churn cut, 150k adds like Verizon +play; 5G mmWave/C-band 12 bps cut, 450Mbps speeds; Smart Retention AI on 500 signals saved 18% at-risk via incentives 3:1 ROI; NBA/NFL windows 15 bps media drop via AWS CDN, sports 85% retention.

Regions: NA 70% subs, U.S. postpaid 0.82% CBRS win, Canada 1.05% Rogers; Europe 20% 1.35% Vodafone merger/EU caps, UK 1.8% BT but JV stable; APAC 10% India 2.1% down Airtel zero-rate, Australia 1.0% NBN; emerging 35% churn focus prepaid conversion.

FY24 target <1.10%, $1.2B capex: 10G PON 40% coverage -20 bps broadband; VIP Rewards gamified 30% uplift McKinsey; Google Cloud edge AI 25% interventions; SpectrumCo migration 15 bps.

This fuels 2-3% revenue, $200+ CLV, $8B+ FY24 FCF ahead of peers.

Lastly, cost of revenue at $17.8 billion, 58% of revenue—120 bps better sequentially, flat YoY. Third straight margin gain from Network Lean, $450 million YTD savings SDN/NFV.

Trends: YoY +1.2% vs. 4.1% revenue; seq +0.8%; normalized -0.5% ex-$150M spectrum.

Buckets: Network Ops 65% $11.57B +0.4%—D&A $4.2B +5% 5G SA/Open RAN like Verizon/Vodafone; cash opex $5.1B -3% AI Nokia AVA energy -12% $180M, 8% power rise; leases $2.27B $75M towerco deals; FTTx 15M homes XGS-PON $220M copper defer.

Content $4.98B -2.1% $110M save—linear 55% -4% Peacock renewals; sports $1.8B flat NBA/NFL to TeleMedia+ $90M; originals $1.2B +3% EchoVerse but $18/sub -6% Netflix-style; CDN Akamai -8% $45M edge/IPv6.

CPE $1.25B +4.5% 5G subs/Wi-Fi7 FWA $80M installment like T-Mobile <0.9% churn, ARPU $52 +2.3%.

Regions: NA 75% $13.35B flat 7% traffic, mmWave 15% GB cost drop; Europe 15% $2.67B +3% energy but roaming/Orange JV 10%; APAC/LATAM 10% $1.78B +5% spectrum but 20% slicing Samsung.

Pivoting asset-light: 40% edge AWS Outposts -25% core, $1B FY25 disagg Huawei white-box. Supply inflation 4%, FCC auctions risks, but $8-10B capex ROIC 12%. 200+ bps FY24 margin to 42%.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage to 85% of top markets, with standalone deployments enhancing speeds to 2 Gbps medians and reducing latency below 5ms. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, with AI optimizations cutting faults by 30% and energy use 22%. We're seeing increased data usage across our customer base, up with genAI and metaverse demands per Ericsson reports. We are also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure through zero-trust SASE and edge computing. Our team's dedication to virtualization and Open RAN has been instrumental in achieving these results, supporting the margin and churn gains highlighted.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Chen: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for churn management going forward?

Alex Rivera: Certainly, Mike. The landscape remains intense with pricing from T-Mobile and cord-cutting pressures, but our integrated bundles like Total Connect have driven churn to 1.12%, best-in-class. We're countering with AI retention tools preventing 18% at-risk losses, exclusive sports content, and 5G upgrades addressing congestion—targeting sub-1.10% in FY24 while peers lag.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact EBITDA margins?

Jordan Lee: We anticipate 1.5-2 million net adds in Q1 2024, driven by FWA and postpaid 5G, adding to ARPU via Unlimited plans. This supports our 39-40.5% margin guide, as bundles lift retention and efficiencies like network virtualization add 200+ bps leverage, with B2B high-margin wins accelerating the trajectory.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Wong: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

Taylor Kim: Absolutely, David. We've accelerated FTTH to 55% coverage with 10G PON, passing 15 million new homes this year, and XGS-PON in JVs like Orange. ROIC on these assets is 14%, above WACC, with FWA synergies yielding 85% gross margins and 20 bps churn cuts. FY24 capex keeps focus here for 40% coverage, targeting 15%+ ROI amid gigabit mandates.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in TeleMedia Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
